subject: tufted titmouse
title: This Little Bird Plucks Hair From Living Dogs, Raccoons and People

scenes.text: A bird smaller than your fist walks up to a raccoon and starts pulling its fur.
It's the tufted titmouse, and it steals hair from animals that are wide awake.
Scientists found only nine studies describing it, so they searched online videos.
The victims: 47 humans, 45 dogs, three cats, three raccoons and one porcupine.
Scientists named it with Greek words for hair theft.
Why? The fur lines its nest, keeps chicks warm, and its smell may keep predators and parasites away. Even a porcupine got robbed.

description:
Tufted titmice pull hair straight off living raccoons, dogs, cats, a porcupine and plenty of people, to line their nests.
Researchers at the University of Illinois found just nine published studies on it, then tallied online videos: 47 humans, 45 dogs, three cats, three raccoons and a porcupine. They called it kleptotrichy (Ecology, 2021). The hair may insulate the nest and repel predators or parasites.
Would you let a bird pluck your hair?
first_comment: The researchers think it is more common further north, where warm nests matter more. Has a bird ever tried this on you?
